daily_reality.summary: Psychiatrists diagnose and treat mental health disorders through medication management, psychotherapy, and consultation. They see 10-20 patients/day in outpatient settings with 15-30 minute medication checks and longer initial evaluations. Telepsychiatry is now a major delivery model.
typical_tasks: Conduct psychiatric evaluations and diagnostic assessments
Prescribe and manage psychotropic medications (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, anxiolytics)
Monitor medication efficacy and side effects in follow-up visits
Review lab results (lithium levels, metabolic panels, drug screens)
Collaborate with primary care, psychologists, social workers, and case managers
Complete clinical documentation in EHR systems
Handle psychiatric emergencies and crisis consultations
Conduct capacity evaluations and involuntary commitment assessments
key_documents: Prescription records and controlled substance logs
Involuntary hold/commitment documentation (5150, Baker Act, etc.)
Informed consent for medications and treatment

deadlines.emergency_response: Immediate for psychiatric emergencies (suicidal patients, acute psychosis)
deadlines.initial_evaluation: 60-90 minute initial evaluation documented same day
deadlines.medication_follow_up: 15-30 minute visits every 1-4 weeks for acute cases
deadlines.prior_authorization: Within 48-72 hours to avoid treatment delays
deadlines.controlled_substance_monitoring: State PDMP check before every controlled substance prescription

daily_reality.seasonality: Increased demand during holiday season (November-January) and seasonal depression periods. Post-pandemic sustained high demand. Summer slightly lower volume due to patient vacations.

regulatory.summary: Psychiatrists require MD/DO degree, 4-year residency, state medical license, DEA registration for controlled substances. Telepsychiatry flexibilities extended through December 2026. Board certification through ABPN is standard.

key_laws.name: DEA Controlled Substances Act — Registration Required
key_laws.status: Active — DEA telemedicine extension through December 2026

key_laws.name: Ryan Haight Online Pharmacy Consumer Protection Act
key_laws.status: Active — modified by COVID telemedicine extensions

key_laws.name: 42 CFR Part 2 — Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Records
key_laws.status: Active — stricter than HIPAA for SUD records

requirements: MD or DO degree from accredited medical school
Board certification through ABPN (American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology)
CME requirements (varies by state, typically 50+ hours per cycle)
State PDMP registration (Prescription Drug Monitoring Program)

regulatory.penalties: Practicing without license: felony in most states. DEA violations: fines up to $500K, imprisonment up to 20 years. HIPAA violations: $100-$50K per incident. Malpractice average settlement: $250K-$400K for psychiatry.
controlling_bodies: ABPN (American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology — certification)
CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services — billing compliance)

tools.summary: Psychiatrists use specialty EHR systems (ICANotes, Valant, SimplePractice), telepsychiatry platforms, e-prescribing tools, and clinical assessment instruments (PHQ-9, GAD-7, DSM-5-TR criteria).

primary_tools.name: ICANotes
primary_tools.description: Leading behavioral health EHR with psychiatry-specific templates and note-writing tools

primary_tools.name: Valant
primary_tools.description: Psychiatry-specific EHR with outcome tracking, measurement-based care dashboards

primary_tools.name: SimplePractice / TherapyNotes
primary_tools.description: Popular practice management and EHR platforms for outpatient psychiatry

primary_tools.name: Telepsychiatry Platforms (Doxy.me, Zoom for Healthcare)
primary_tools.description: HIPAA-compliant video platforms for remote psychiatric consultations

primary_tools.name: E-Prescribing (EPCS) Systems
primary_tools.description: Electronic prescribing of controlled substances — required in most states

secondary_tools: PHQ-9, GAD-7, AUDIT — standardized screening instruments
State PDMP portals — prescription drug monitoring
AIMS (Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale) for tardive dyskinesia monitoring
UpToDate / Lexicomp — clinical decision support and drug references
pain_points: Excessive prior authorization requirements for medications
EHR documentation burden — 2+ hours/day on notes for some psychiatrists
Poor interoperability between behavioral health and medical EHRs
Complex controlled substance prescribing regulations varying by state
Insurance reimbursement rates not keeping pace with demand

terminology.summary: Psychiatry uses DSM-5-TR diagnostic criteria, psychopharmacology terminology, and clinical assessment jargon. Unique combination of medical and psychological terminology.

terms.DSM-5-TR: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition, Text Revision — the standard diagnostic reference
terms.ASD: Autism Spectrum Disorder (or Acute Stress Disorder depending on context)
terms.PRN: Pro re nata — as needed (medication dosing)
terms.5150: California involuntary psychiatric hold (72 hours) — used colloquially nationwide
terms.anhedonia: Inability to experience pleasure — key symptom of depression
terms.anosognosia: Lack of insight into one's illness

career_psychology.summary: 12-year training pathway (undergrad + med school + residency). Average salary $360K-$382K with strong growth. Severe national shortage (43,660 projected by 2038) creates excellent job security. High burnout risk from emotional burden and administrative load.
career_path: Medical school — MD or DO (4 years)
Optional fellowship (1-2 years: child/adolescent, addiction, forensic, geriatric, etc.)
Medical Director / Department Chair / Academic faculty
fears: Patient suicide — most dreaded outcome in psychiatry
Violence from patients in acute settings
Malpractice suits related to medication side effects or missed diagnoses
Burnout from emotional burden and vicarious trauma
motivation: Transforming lives of patients with severe mental illness
Strong job security due to massive national shortage
Growing societal acceptance and destigmatization of mental health
Flexible practice models (telepsychiatry, part-time, locum tenens)
Intellectually stimulating — intersection of neuroscience, psychology, and medicine
burnout_factors: Emotional burden of treating severely ill and suicidal patients
High caseloads in community mental health settings (250-500 patients)
Stigma within medicine — psychiatry historically undervalued by peers
Isolation — often sole psychiatrist in a practice or facility

community.summary: Highly organized professional community led by the American Psychiatric Association (APA). Multiple subspecialty organizations. APA Annual Meeting is the flagship event (16,000+ attendees).

associations.name: American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (AACAP)
American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN)
American Association for Academic Psychiatry (AAP)
associations.type: Organization for academic psychiatrists and educators

events: APA Annual Meeting 2026 (May 16-20, San Francisco — Moscone Center)
APA Institute on Psychiatric Services (annual, fall)
online_communities: Doximity — physician social network with psychiatry groups

market.summary: Severe psychiatrist shortage in the US — 43,660 projected deficit by 2038. Average salary $360K-$382K in 2026. 12.5% employment growth projected through 2032. Telepsychiatry expanding access and compensation.

job_outlook.growth_rate: 12.5% projected through 2032 (BLS) — much faster than average
job_outlook.demand_drivers: Mental health crisis, aging population, destigmatization, telehealth access

market_trends: Telepsychiatry as standard care delivery model — DEA extensions through 2026
Collaborative care models embedding psychiatrists in primary care
Growing subspecialty demand in addiction psychiatry (opioid crisis)
Child/adolescent psychiatry shortage even more severe than adult
Measurement-based care and AI-assisted diagnostics emerging
Psychedelic-assisted therapy (psilocybin, MDMA) creating new treatment paradigms
